title: Alaska Safe Families and Villages Act of 2014
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the Senate on December 9, 2014. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Amends the Violence Against Women Reauthorization Act of 2013 to repeal a provision prohibiting Alaska tribes other than the Metlakatla Indian Community from issuing and enforcing domestic violence protective orders against non-member Alaska Natives and non-Natives.

summary.headline: A 2014 law lets most Alaska tribes issue and enforce domestic violence protective orders against non-members, including non-Natives, by repealing a earlier restriction.
summary.what_it_does: Before this law, the Violence Against Women Reauthorization Act of 2013 barred Alaska tribes other than the Metlakatla Indian Community from issuing and enforcing domestic violence protective orders against non-member Alaska Natives and non-Natives. This law repeals that restriction. As a result, those tribes may now issue and enforce such orders against non-members.

who_it_affects.group: Alaska tribes other than the Metlakatla Indian Community
who_it_affects.how: They gain authority to issue and enforce domestic violence protective orders against non-member Alaska Natives and non-Natives.

who_it_affects.group: Non-member Alaska Natives and non-Natives subject to tribal domestic violence protective orders
who_it_affects.how: They can now be subject to protective orders issued and enforced by Alaska tribes, which previously was not allowed.

who_it_affects.group: Victims of domestic violence in Alaska tribal communities
who_it_affects.how: Tribes can use protective orders against non-members who commit domestic violence, which the summary describes as a new option for tribal courts.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 18, 2014; the official summary does not state a separate effective date.
